note: Fresh unseen scenario from another family: diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care gastric ultrasound in patients taking GLP-1 receptor agonists. Written 2026-09-22 after the build was frozen; never used during development.

inputs.need: More of our elective surgical patients now take GLP-1 receptor agonists such as semaglutide, and we have had two cases of regurgitated solid food at induction despite normal fasting. Some anaesthetists already do point-of-care gastric ultrasound before induction, but we do not know how well it identifies a stomach that still holds solids or a large fluid volume in these patients. I want to measure how accurate bedside gastric ultrasound is in patients on GLP-1 receptor agonists, against a reference standard we can defend.
inputs.constraints: Two trained sonographers among the anaesthetists. No extra fasting beyond the current guideline. Gastroscopy is only available for patients already booked for upper endoscopy. About 18 months to finish.
localFacts: The endoscopy unit performs about 30 upper endoscopies a week under anaesthesia care, and the unit lead agreed on 2026-09-12 that suctioned gastric volume can be measured and recorded (email EU-2026-044).
Two anaesthetists hold gastric ultrasound certification from a recognised course.

steps.fallbackQuery: ("gastric ultrasound" OR "gastric ultrasonography" OR "point-of-care ultrasound") AND ("GLP-1" OR semaglutide OR "glucagon-like peptide")
